Load a creel's design tables from an API connection

Source: R/fetch-design.R
fetch_design.Rd

Many agency creel APIs serve the survey's own design alongside its data: the season, the shift windows with their selection probabilities, the sections and the special dates. fetch_design() reads them through the same profile as the data, renames them to canonical columns and returns them as a list, so a calendar can be built from what the design says rather than recomputed by hand.

Like every other endpoint, the design endpoints and their field names are the caller's to declare: add design_general, design_periods and, optionally, design_sections and design_special_dates to endpoints and to api_field_map (or the profile's endpoints: and field_map:).

Usage

fetch_design(conn, ...)

Arguments

conn

A creel_connection created by creel_connect_api() or creel_connect_from_yaml().

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

A named list of data frames, each with creel_uid, the creel UID it was fetched for:

  • general: one row per creel. season_start, season_end (Date), and the special-date rule as two logical flags: special_as_stratum (special dates form strata of their own) and special_as_weekend (special dates join the weekend), each carried when mapped.

  • periods: one row per month and period. month (integer), period_id (character), start_time, end_time (character, "HH:MM"), length_hours (numeric, from the clock times), crosses_midnight (logical), p_period (numeric, in (0, 1]), and stored_length_hours when the source stores one.

  • sections: section (character), or NULL when no design_sections endpoint is configured.

  • special_dates: date (Date) and group (character, when mapped), or NULL when no design_special_dates endpoint is configured.

Shift lengths

Each period's length is computed from its start and end clock times, adding a day when the end is not after the start: a shift that crosses midnight. The length the source stores is kept beside it as stored_length_hours, and every period where the two disagree is reported with a warning (creel_warning_design_length_disagrees) rather than one silently preferred. A stored length computed as end - start on a clock that wraps (a 19:30-00:30 shift stored as -19 h) has reached published reports; this is the check that catches it. crosses_midnight marks the shifts that make a night design (see tidycreel::creel_design()).

These are the real shift lengths. tidycreel divides by p_period itself, so a length already divided by the probability must never be passed to tidycreel::add_counts().
